script.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

epidemiology.who: Any age, often first found in adolescents and young adults; the most common inherited heart disease (about 1 in 500) and a leading cause of sudden death in young athletes
risk_factors: family history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or sudden death
a sarcomere gene variant, most often in beta-myosin heavy chain or myosin-binding protein C

script.pathophysiology: A variant in a sarcomere protein causes asymmetric hypertrophy of the left ventricle, usually of the septum, with disorganized myocytes (myocyte disarray). The stiff ventricle fills poorly. In the obstructive form, the anterior mitral leaflet is pulled toward the septum in systole (systolic anterior motion), obstructing outflow and causing mitral regurgitation.

timeline.onset: Often appears in adolescence or early adulthood
timeline.course: Variable: many live normal lives, but some develop sudden death, heart failure or atrial fibrillation

history: sudden death may be the first sign
exam: systolic ejection murmur at the left lower sternal border that gets louder with Valsalva or standing and softer with squatting or handgrip
imaging: echocardiogram showing a septum 15 mm or thicker, often with systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve
cardiac MRI showing hypertrophy and fibrosis
ECG with left ventricular hypertrophy and deep Q waves

criteria: Left ventricular wall thickness of 15 mm or more (13 mm or more with a family history), not explained by another cause

first_line: ICD for patients at high risk of sudden death
screen first-degree relatives with ECG and echocardiogram
next_line: verapamil or diltiazem if beta blockers fail
mavacamten, a cardiac myosin inhibitor, for obstructive symptoms
septal reduction: surgical myectomy or alcohol septal ablation

complications: sudden cardiac death from ventricular arrhythmia

confused_with.how_to_tell_apart: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy causes a systolic murmur at the left lower sternal border that gets louder with Valsalva or standing; the murmur of aortic stenosis radiates to the carotids and gets softer. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is inherited and shows up in the young; aortic stenosis is a disease of older adults.

pearls: Anything that shrinks the ventricle (Valsalva, standing, dehydration) makes the obstruction and murmur worse; squatting and handgrip make them softer.
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.
Systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve also causes mitral regurgitation.

sources.title: 2024 AHA/ACC/AMSSM/HRS/PACES/SCMR Guideline for the Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of cardiomyopathies
